claims.quote: War  has  been  possible,  no  doubt,  but it  has  at  last  become  impossible,  and  those  who  are  preparing for  war,  and  basing  all  their  schemes  of  life  on  the expectation  of  war,  are  visionaries  of  the  worst  kind,  for war  is  no  longer  possible.
claims.description: Great wars between major powers have become impossible.

claims.quote: and  it  is  that  war  which,  I  maintain,  has  become  absolutely impossible.
claims.description: A general European war between the Triple Alliance and the Franco-Russian Alliance cannot happen.

claims.quote: Thus,  the great  war  cannot  be  made,  and  any  attempt  to  make  it would  result  in  suicide.
claims.description: Any attempt at a great war would end in catastrophe, destroying existing political organizations.

claims.quote: I  think  it  can  be  mathematically demonstrated  that,  in  future,  war  will  be  decided at  ranges  which  will  render  the  use  of  the  bayonet  impossible.
claims.description: Future battles will be fought at ranges that make the bayonet obsolete.

claims.quote: In  his  eyes  the  bayonet  is  supreme,  and  it  is cold  steel  which  at  the  last  will  always  be  the  deciding factor  in  the  combats  of  peopies.
claims.description: General Dragomiroff holds that the bayonet will always decide future battles.

claims.quote: whether  in future  combatants  will  ever  be  able  to  get  within  one hundred  yards  of  one  another,  let  alone  one  yard.
claims.description: Future combatants may never be able to close within a hundred yards of each other.

claims.quote: They  are,  indeed,  becoming  so  deadly that  before  long  you  will  see  they  will  never  fight  at  all.
claims.description: Weapons will become so deadly that nations will stop fighting altogether.

claims.quote: he  relied  for the  extinction  of  war  upon  the  invention  of  a  machine which  would  infallibly  slay  fifty  per  cent,  of  the  combatants whenever  battle  was  waged.
claims.description: Kipling hopes for a weapon so lethal (killing half of all combatants) that war would end by itself.

claims.quote: in which  he  attributed  the  final  disappearance  of  war  from the  planet  to  the  discovery  of  vril,  a  destructive  so  deadly that  an  army  could  be  annihilated  by  the  touch  of  a button  by  the  finger  of  a  child.
claims.description: Lytton's 'vril', a push-button weapon able to annihilate an army, ends war on the planet.

claims.quote: They  will  never  again face  the  fire  of  modern  rifles.
claims.description: The Dervishes, having been slaughtered at Omdurman, will never again face modern rifle fire.

claims.quote: one  or  two experiences  of  that  kind  will  rid  our  military  authorities of  any  desire  to  come  to  close  quarters  with  their adversaries.
claims.description: After one or two massacres, European armies will give up close-quarters attacks.

claims.quote: At  first  there will  be  increased  slaughter — increased  slaughter  on  so terrible  a  scale  as  to  render  it  impossible  to  get  troops  to push  the  battle  to  a  decisive  issue.
claims.description: A future great war will begin with slaughter so terrible that troops cannot be driven to a decisive result.

claims.quote: Then,  instead  of  a  war  fought  out  to the  bitter  end  in  a  series  of  decisive  battles,  we  shall  have as  a  substitute  a  long  period  of  continually  increasing strain  upon  the  resources  of  the  combatants.
claims.description: Future war becomes a long war of attrition that drains the combatants' resources instead of decisive battles.

claims.quote: will  become  a  kind  of  stalemate,  in  which  neither  army being  able  to  get  at  the  other,  both  armies  will  be maintained  in  opposition  to  each  other
claims.description: Future war becomes an entrenched stalemate in which neither army can reach the other or deliver a decisive attack.

claims.quote: accompanied  by  entire  dislocation of  all  industry  and  severing  of  all  the  sources  of  supply by  which  alone  the  community  is  enabled  to  bear  the crushing  burden  of  that  armed  peace.
claims.description: A future war will dislocate all industry and cut off supply.

claims.quote: That  is  the  future  of  war— not  fighting,  but famine,  not  the  slaying  of  men,  but  the  bankruptcy  of nations  and  the  break-up  of  the  whole  social  organisation.
claims.description: Future war will mean famine, national bankruptcy and the collapse of social order rather than battle.

claims.quote: The  soldier  by  natural  evolution  has  so  perfected  the mechanism  of  slaughter  that  he  has  practically  secured his  own  extinction.
claims.description: Soldiers have made weapons so deadly and costly that the soldier will become extinct.

claims.quote: Now  armies  will  no  longer  fight  in  the  dark.
claims.description: Smokeless powder will leave battlefields unobscured, so soldiers see the full carnage around them.

claims.quote: In  the  warfare  of  the  future  men  will  simply  fall  and die  without  either  seeing  or  hearing  anything.
claims.description: In future war soldiers will be killed by unseen, unheard fire from distant marksmen.

claims.quote: only  after  some  time  will  they  be  able  to discover  that  the  invisible  shafts  of  death  were  sped  from a  line  of  sharp-shooters  lying  invisible  at  a  distance  of  a mile  or  more.
claims.description: Hidden riflemen will kill from a mile or more away with no visible sign of where the fire comes from.

claims.quote: The  ordinary  soldier will  fire  twelve  times  as  many  shots  per  minute  as  he was  able  to  do  in  1870,  and  even  this  is  likely  to  be rapidly  improved  upon.
claims.description: Infantry rate of fire, already twelve times that of 1870, will rise rapidly further.

claims.quote: the  rifle  of to-morrow  will  be  forty  times  as  effective  as  the  chassepot was  in  the  Franco-Prussian  war.
claims.description: The rifle of tomorrow will be forty times as effective as the 1870 Chassepot.

claims.quote: With  a  bullet  of 4  mm.  he  will  carry  380,  and  when  we  have  a  rifle  of 3  mm.  calibre  he  will  be  able  to  take  575  into  action,  and not  have  to  carry  any  more  weight  than  that  which burdened  him  when  he  carried  84,  twenty  years  ago.
claims.description: Smaller-calibre rifles will let each soldier carry hundreds more cartridges for the same weight (575 with a 3 mm rifle).

claims.quote: but  the  3  mm.  gun  will  probably  be the  gun  of  the  future,  for  the  increased  impetus  of  the small  bore  and  its  advantage  in  lightness  will  compel  its adoption.
claims.description: A 3 mm small-bore rifle will probably become the standard military rifle.
